B. Is this measure already running in Kanta-Häme wellbeing services county (or in the Tays university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
effect_summary_en: One small English before-after study from 2004 found that the yearly resection rate rose by 30% after video MDT meetings with a thoracic surgeon began. It did not measure the share of all patients who got curative treatment.
supported_en: A 2004 Southend–London study (Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare) reports a 30% relative rise in the yearly resection rate after telemedicine MDT meetings began (62 patients in one year).
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the assumed gain of 1.5 percentage points in the curative share, and they include no recent or Finnish data.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found that every stage I–III lung cancer patient from Kanta-Häme is discussed by video with the Tays lung team before curative treatment is ruled out. Pages only describe general multidisciplinary meetings and cooperation with Tays.
summary_en: B: Tays Cancer Centre says weekly multidisciplinary meetings (MDT meetings) draw up treatment recommendations, and says Kanta-Häme Central Hospital works closely with Tays, including in multidisciplinary meetings. No page read says that every stage I–III lung cancer patient from Kanta-Häme is reviewed by video with the Tays lung team. A: The only effect evidence is a 2004 English before-after study, where the yearly resection rate rose by 30% after video MDT meetings began.
unanswered_en: No page read said whether Kanta-Häme lung cancer patients are routinely presented to the Tays lung cancer MDT by video; an old page on the former Kanta-Häme hospital district site (khshp.fi) about doctors' meetings with Tays was found but not read, and no Finnish data on the effect were found.
